pxt_behavior: Archive content matches the respective Microsoft PXT GitHub release tags exactly: 1102/1102 and 1271/1271 files, no changed, missing or added members after normalizing container roots. Manifest package.json identity/version and declared command scripts corroborate Microsoft MakeCode/PXT educational compiler/editor sources.

Application StartPage points at MakeCode; included rules grant WinRT API access to named MakeCode sites and localhost:3232 development pages. This is a real authority surface, retained as suspicious; a declaration alone establishes neither token theft nor an AppContainer escape.

pxtwinrt/winrt.ts initializes serial support only in WinRT, captures file activation, reads the selected HEX file and imports its unpacked source. winrtworkspace.ts creates an app-local target folder and reads/writes project packages beneath it.

pxtwinrt/deploy.ts enumerates removable devices, filters configured board display names and writes compiled firmware; saveOnlyAsync uses FileSavePicker. browserDownloadAsync writes a temporary exported file and invokes Windows.System.Launcher.launchFileAsync. These filesystem and execution capabilities remain notable.
pxtwinrt/serial.ts opens matching board serial devices through SerialDevice.fromIdAsync, reads their streams, and posts serial messages to the app. It is board I/O, not keyboard spying.

cli/server.ts defaults to localhost, checks a local authorization token and dispatches project/HID/serial development operations. cli/cli.ts uses keytar for user-supplied pxt/github/crowdin account tokens and invokes compiler/build/publish tools. Electron updater stages an update installer in its cache and launches it from quitAndInstall. These are developer/editor functions.

external/tdast.js is the shared 4.96 MB TouchDevelop AST/compiler/runtime. CompiledScript.init and reinit evaluate supplied compiled program code and register the resulting runtime functions. This is a supported interpreter capability. Vendor bundles are minified/transpiled; no concealed malicious stage was established by tracing these paths.
pxt_balance: Complete upstream content agreement plus coherent editor/compiler, project-storage and board-deployment paths tip both archives to BENIGN. They retain dangerous capabilities and HTTP development-origin declarations. No installed-site integrity, deployment authorization, or runtime security guarantee is inferred. Several large/generated source files have recorded flow-analysis limits; absence of alarms is not the verdict basis.
killwin_behavior: 154-byte, unobfuscated four-line Windows batch source; the .fr suffix does not itself execute. When passed to cmd, execution falls through all three deletion commands without a guard or recovery branch.

@echo off disables command echo. del "%SystemRoot%\system32\*.dll" /q requests a quiet wildcard deletion of system DLLs. The subsequent del removes the Driver Cache\i386\driver.cab cabinet with /f /q, then removes system32\devmgmt.msc.

Each command redirects stdout to NUL; stderr is not redirected. There is no network transfer, payload stage, persistence, credential access, elevation attempt, secure erasure or self-delete in the complete source.

The combination of indiscriminate OS DLL deletion and removal of driver-repair material and Device Manager tips the judgement to MALICIOUS. Invocation, privileges and file-protection outcomes are unknown; hostile intent does not require observing success. Existing three hostile traits cover the three distinct supported destructive outcomes.
